```{r}
library(jsonlite)
s <- read_json("feasibility.json",simplifyVector=TRUE)
stopifnot(s$status=="unavailable",s$source_unchanged,s$clinical_models_fitted==0)
Sys.setenv(BMI_REPO_ROOT=normalizePath("../.."))
source("../../R/analysis.R")
dir.create("figures",showWarnings=FALSE)
positions<-data.frame(model_id=paste0("primary::paired_abg/encounter/",c("hypercapnia","acidemic_hypercapnia"),"/spline"),status="Source unavailable",probability=NA_real_,n_model=NA_real_,n_reference=NA_real_)
a <- list(pairing_status=data.frame(status=s$status,reason=s$reason),probability_curves=positions,model_registry=data.frame(),distribution_bins=data.frame())
caption <- bmi_paired_figure(list(analysis=a,manifest=list(mode="source_audit")),"figures")
write.csv(caption,"figures/captions.csv",row.names=FALSE)
```

## Finding

**The paired-ABG acidemia analysis is unavailable for this accepted source.**
Ordinary arterial PCO~2~ and arterial pH records exist, but their same-sample linkage
cannot be authenticated. Encounter/date co-occurrence is insufficient. No clinical
supplemental models, paired prevalences or supplemental PIFs have been estimated.
The existing clinical results and selected B/F2 figures are unchanged.

## What was checked

The narrow read-only query used the pinned accepted-source reader and original
patient/encounter keys for **`r format(s$n_input_encounters,big.mark=',')` study-input
encounters**. It retained ordinary arterial PCO~2~ (LOINC 2019-8), arterial pH
(2744-1), and selected adjusted/venous/unspecified comparator codes for audit.
It did not rebuild preprocessing, change the index, select a later encounter or
pair by record order. The source, input, manifest and configuration identities
were stable during extraction. Event identifiers and dates remain private.

```{r}
labels<-c(candidate_records="Queried gas records",ordinary_arterial_pco2_records="Ordinary arterial PCO2 records",arterial_ph_records="Arterial pH records",date_only_records="Records with date-only precision",specimen_id_populated="Populated specimen identifiers",panel_id_populated="Populated panel identifiers",accession_id_populated="Populated accession identifiers",collection_time_populated="Populated collection times",result_status_populated="Populated result_status fields",result_version_populated="Populated result_version fields")
knitr::kable(data.frame(Quantity=unname(labels),Records=format(unlist(s$aggregate_counts[names(labels)]),big.mark=",",trim=TRUE)),row.names=FALSE)
```

These are record counts, not distinct blood draws or patient prevalences. The
arterial analyte counts cannot be added to infer pairs. Generic `status` and `order_status` columns exist, but their correction semantics
are unreviewed; the dedicated status/version counts above do not establish that
all status information is absent. Unique specimens, valid
pairs, unpaired measurements, ambiguous links and endpoint prevalence are **not
assessable**, not zero. All supplied pairing states are source-unavailable.

## Planned analysis and unavailable positions

Two secondary positions are implemented: any valid pair with PaCO~2~ ≥45 mm Hg,
and any same pair also having pH <7.35. They retain identical patients and pairs,
primary numeric spline knots, inherited adjustment and the original index.
No pair means unknown, not a negative endpoint. The software retains explicit
unavailable model positions without changing the existing analysis.

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Supplement S1. Both secondary curves and the paired-population distribution are unavailable because this source cannot establish same-sample arterial PCO2 and pH. Empty positions do not indicate zero risk or zero patients. No clinical curve is drawn."
#| out-width: 100%
knitr::include_graphics(paste0("figures/S1-paired-ABG.",if(knitr::is_latex_output())"pdf"else"png"))
```

## What would permit estimation

A future source would need authenticated, source-scoped same-sample identifiers
(or independently validated unique collection-time linkage), reviewed ordinary
arterial pH units and validity bounds, and documented duplicate/correction rules.
The inherited producer's exclusive 6.5–7.8 pH screen was identified, but no new
clinical pairing policy has been approved. This is a specific source limitation,
not a request to replace the accepted dataset or permission to approximate pairs.

Even with valid pairs, acidemia would not establish acute respiratory failure;
absence would not establish compensation. Treatment timing and selection into
paired measurement would remain limitations. Separate fitted curves can cross
and would be flagged without clipping or substituting another estimator.

## Evidence and review status

The accompanying `feasibility.json` contains source/input identity hashes and the
complete aggregate counters. The private extraction and additive-enrichment
receipts remain on the Mini. The original clinical snapshot remains in
`results/2026-10-18/`. Software tests, numerical verification, visual inspection and
investigator interpretation are distinct; this report does not grant new
scientific or submission approval. No abstract has been drafted.
